description:
Found by the HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9, docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy.md, point 7). An alloc inside a loop allocates on every iteration and nothing is freed until the kernel returns (language.md 'Allocating'); for a per-window scratch histogram over a 1 GB input that is 512 MB. defk-djy.9 added it to getting-started 'Things that trip people up' with a checked example (scratch array before the loop, cleared each pass). The report (Defk.Report.print/1, __defk_report__/0) could flag it where the author looks when tuning.

Done when the fast-path report notes each alloc that sits inside a loop body (with the loop and a one-line suggestion to hoist it and clear it per pass), __defk_report__/0 carries it as data, a report test covers it, and docs/fast-path-report.md lists the note.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Add a hoisting suggestion to the fast-path report's alloc-inside-a-loop note

**Current behavior:**
Since defk-4b2 the fast-path report already notes every `alloc/2` or value-semantics copy inside a loop body, as the fact `{:owned, :per_iteration, text}` in `__defk_report__/0`, printed by `Defk.Report.print/1`/`format/1` and listed in docs/fast-path-report.md. The alloc text reads "alloc/2 is inside a loop: each iteration keeps a buffer until the kernel returns (max_owned bounds the total)". It says what goes wrong but not what to do, which is the part the HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9, point 7) asked for.

**Desired behavior:**
The note for an `alloc/2` inside a loop also gives a one-line fix in the same words getting-started's "Things that trip people up" uses: allocate it once before the loop and clear it each pass. The note for a copy keeps its current text (hoisting is not the fix for a copy). The fact's shape `{:owned, :per_iteration, text}` and where it is attached (the alloc's line) stay the same.

**Key interfaces:**
- `__defk_report__/0` fact `{:owned, :per_iteration, text}`: only `text` changes, and only for alloc/2
- `Defk.Report.format/1` output: shows the new text
- docs/fast-path-report.md: its description of the `:owned` topic mentions the suggestion

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A kernel with `alloc/2` inside a loop body gets an `:owned` note whose text includes the hoist-and-clear suggestion
- [ ] A copy inside a loop gets a note without that suggestion (text unchanged)
- [ ] An alloc outside any loop still gets no `:owned` note
- [ ] The existing owned-budget report tests are updated and pass; `mix test`, `mix docs` and `mix credo --strict` are clean

**Out of scope:**
- Naming or locating the enclosing loop in the note (the alloc's line is enough)
- Any change to the max_owned budget, the copy analysis or freeing buffers early (defk-c1e)
- New report topics or verdicts

title: Fast-path report: note an alloc inside a loop (allocated every pass, freed at return)
